_readme: Named track sections for the Row 5 location readout.
Matching: an entry applies when ANY 'match' substring appears in iRacing's
TrackName or TrackDisplayName (case-insensitive). If 'configs' is non-empty,
some 'configs' key must additionally appear — as a whole word — in
TrackConfigName or in the TrackName slug. iRacing names the layout in the
config on multi-config venues ('Road Course') but only in the slug on
single-config content ('imola gp', empty config); whole-word matching keeps
'gp' from hitting 'gpshort'. An entry with an empty 'configs' list applies
to every layout of the venue; a config-specific entry wins over a
config-agnostic one. Real slugs for most layouts are listed in
Planning/iracing-track-identities.json; tools/validate_track_catalog.py
checks this file against them.
Sections: ordered by 'pct', the fraction of lap distance (iRacing LapDistPct,
0 = start/finish line) where the section begins. Each section runs until the
next one starts; the last section wraps around to the first. Boundaries are
placed slightly BEFORE the corner so the name reads out during the approach
and braking zone, when the driver can still use it.
The pct values are hand-estimated from track maps and meant to be tuned:
turn on Debug Mode and Row 5 shows the live LapDistPct beside the section
name, so you can read the true fraction at each corner off a replay and
adjust the numbers here. No recompile needed.
Attribution: measured turn/straight names and lap-fraction positions in
entries marked source 'lovely-track-data' (and boundary calibration of the
curated entries) come from Lovely Sim Racing's lovely-track-data project,
https://github.com/Lovely-Sim-Racing/lovely-track-data — (c) Lovely Sim
Racing (https://lsr.gg), licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Imported via
tools/import_track_sections.py; re-run it to pick up upstream updates.
